title: Unilateral IRI induction in pigs
projectDescription: Induction of protein PTMs was investigated in a porcine model of unilateral IRI
sampleProcessingProtocol: Kidney cortex tissue was homogenized using a bullet blender in 6M guanidine buffer (6M GuaHCl, 100mM HEPES, 5mM EDTA, 1xRoche complete proteinase inhibitor) at 95°C for 5min. Samples were reduced with 10mM dithiothreitol (30 min., 37 °C) and alkylated with 50mM chloroacetamide (30 min., RT, dark). 100µg protein was precipitated to paramagnetic beads for single-pot solid-phase-enhanced sample preparation (SP3) with 80% EtOH. The precleared proteins were digested with trypsin at a 1:100 protease:protein ratio and subsequently the peptides were purified and enriched using stop-and-go-extraction tips (StageTips). Samples were separated by an Ultimate 3000 nanoflow-HPLC-MS/MS (Thermo Scientific, MA, USA) coupled to a Quadrupole-Orbitrap Exploris480 mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific) with a FAIMS (High Field Asymmetric Waveform Ion Mobility Spectrometry) Pro device attached. Separation was performed in a two-column setup with a PepMap100 C18 trap column (2cm, 75µm ID, 3Å, Thermo Fisher Scientific, MA, USA) and an IonOpticks Gen.2 Aurora 25cm column (IonOpticks, Australia), operated at 50°C within a column oven. An effective separation window of 120min was run from 2% to 30% B (A: water with 0.1% formic acid (v/v), B: acetonitrile with 0.1% formic acid (v/v)) followed by washout (90% B) and re-equilibration. MS data acquisition was performed by Xcalibur 4.4.16.14 (Thermo Scientific, MA, USA) in DDA mode (data dependent acquisition) with FAIMS operating at a total carrier gas flow of 3.8L/min and three compensation voltages (CVs) of  40,  55, and  70V. The ion transfer tube temperature was set to 275°C and the spray voltage to 1500V. The AGC Target for MS1 was set to 300% (normalized) with a RF lens setting of 40% and a scan range of 350-1350m/z. MS1 survey scans were performed at a resolution of 120000 and MS2 scans at a resolution of 15000 (100% normalized AGC target, 28% normalized HCD collision energy) with 1.5s cycle time at -40V and 0.75s cycle time each at -55 and -70V CVs.
dataProcessingProtocol: RAW files were converted with the FAIMS MzXML Generator tool35 (v1.0.7639) into separate MzXML files for each CV of -40, -55, and -70V and queried with MaxQuant36 (v1.6.17.0) against the proteome database for pig (UniProt release 2021-04, 46219 entries) at a FDR of 0.01 using standard settings for Orbitrap instruments (match between runs was enabled). Cysteine carbamidomethylation (+57.021464) were set as a fixed modification, whereas methionine oxidation (+15.994914) and protein N-terminal acetylation (+42.010565) were set as variable modifications. Search results were analyzed with Perseus37 (v1.6.14.0). ) and result ows were filtered for contaminants and reverse sequences. For peptides appearing in at least two groups log2-transformation and Student's t-test were performed. MS Fragger open The open search feature of FragPipe (v17.1, MSFragger v3.4) was used for the of DDA data was used to determine lysine-dependent posttranslational modifications (search window -150 to 500 Da, with trypsin specificity and two allowed missed cleavages). Cysteine carbamidomethylation (+57.021464) was set as a fixed modification and methionine oxidation (+15.994914) as well as protein N-terminal acetylation (+42.010565) were set as variable modifications.
